name: Striate Palmoplantar Keratoderma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Histopathological Diagnostic Criteria for Striate Palmoplantar Keratoderma

criteria.description: Presence of linear or striate hyperkeratotic plaques predominantly on the palms and soles
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Skin biopsy showing epidermal hyperkeratosis with focal parakeratosis and acanthosis
Identification of pathogenic variants in desmoglein 1 (DSG1), desmoplakin (DSP), or plakoglobin (JUP) genes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic clinical features with either positive family history or histopathological confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing can confirm diagnosis but is not mandatory.

laboratory: Histopathology showing epidermal hyperkeratosis with focal parakeratosis and acanthosis
genetic: Pathogenic variants in DSG1, DSP, or JUP genes associated with autosomal dominant inheritance
other: Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant pattern

distinguishingFeatures: Diffuse rather than striate pattern of keratoderma
More uniform thickening of entire palms and soles
Multiple small punctate keratotic lesions instead of linear plaques
Lesions often scattered rather than linear

redFlags: Rapid progression of keratoderma with ulceration
Development of painful fissures with secondary infection
Signs of systemic involvement or syndromic features
references: Richard G et al. Striate palmoplantar keratoderma: clinical and molecular aspects. J Invest Dermatol. 2017.
Orphanet: Striate palmoplantar keratoderma. Orphanet Report Series. 2023.
Smith FJD et al. Mutations in desmoglein 1 cause striate palmoplantar keratoderma. Nat Genet. 2003.
